defects.defect: Two owners of "read the colour out of the URL"; the router-side reader is inert at boot (vue-router's initial navigation is asynchronous, so `route.query` is empty during App setup) and its result is logically subsumed by the hydration source, making the `!appliedFromUrl` guard term unable to change any branch.
defects.evidence: Reader 1: demo/color-picker/composables/boot/hydrate.ts:51-61 hand-parses the hash with URLSearchParams, requires both space+color. Reader 2: demo/color-session/useColorUrl.ts:26-31 reads route.query.space/color, requires both. hydrate.ts:49-50's stated justification ("runs before router installation") is false — index.html:211 `app.use(router)` precedes :212 `app.mount()`, so App setup runs after installation. The real mechanism: node_modules/vue-router/dist/vue-router.js:1462-1466 starts the initial navigation with `push(routerHistory.location)` — a Promise — inside `install`, so `currentRoute.value` is still START_LOCATION_NORMALIZED (query {}) when App's setup runs synchronously inside app.mount(). Hence useColorUrl.ts:70 `const appliedFromUrl = applyUrlToModel()` is false on every cold load. Subsumption: both readers require both params, so appliedFromUrl===true ⟹ hydration.source==="url", and App.vue:378 `if (!appliedFromUrl && hydration.source !== "url")` already gates on the latter.
defects.mechanism: dual ownership of one concept, one instance vestigial after a transposition
defects.reproduction: Deterministic source read, both halves: vue-router.js:1462-1466 (async navigation start) + index.html:210-212 (synchronous mount ordering) + the conjunct-subsumption argument over hydrate.ts:51-61 vs useColorUrl.ts:26-31.
defects.proposedCure: hydrate.ts owns the FIRST value (already correct); useColorUrl owns the LIVE sync only — delete its boot-time applyUrlToModel() call and the appliedFromUrl return, and reduce App.vue:378 to `if (hydration.source !== "url") restoreFromStorage();`. One owner per phase. Correct hydrate.ts:49-50's rationale to the real one (the router's initial navigation is a promise) — that is the fact a future reader needs.

defects.defect: App.vue's boot contract is split across a file it does not own and duplicated in two languages. (1) `class="relative"` is DEAD: the atmosphere canvas (App.vue:9-17, `absolute inset-0`) is a descendant of `.app-layout` (App.vue:2) which is already `position: relative` (shell.css:25), so the nearest positioned ancestor is never `<body>` — a legacy positioning ancestor, owner edict 2. (2) `data-paper-field` is glass-ui's field contract governing App.vue's own descendants incl. portalled dialogs (index.html:222-226) yet is declared where App.vue cannot see it. (3) Mount replaces the host's children, so `<body>` can hold no `<noscript>` and no pre-rendered fallback — while VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:168 requires "A static semantic boot-error region already present in HTML becomes visible through that data state"; measured groundState=null confirms the whole §6.2 latch (data-ground-state / -schema / -store) is unimplemented. (4) index.html:180-200 runs URL/storage/default precedence in vanilla JS writing --saved-bg-0..N; App.vue:231 `resolveHydratedBootModel()` runs URL->storage->default AGAIN in TypeScript (boot/hydrate.ts:53-78) — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:172: "The hydrated model consumes the frozen boot object ...; it does not repeat scheme/URL/storage precedence, reconstruct an initial palette in TypeScript, or repaint a second 'equivalent' ground."
defects.mechanism: split root ownership — the component's own root contract (positioning ancestor, material attribute, boot precedence) lives in the entry HTML, so it is untyped, untestable, invisible to the component, and duplicated
defects.reproduction: node <scratchpad>/probe-app-D.mjs  → every row: mountHostIsBody true, appLayoutParent "body", bodyAttrs 'class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field=""', groundState null. Then: `.app-layout` becomes the app's own root and already declares position:relative, so `class="relative"` is DELETED not moved; `data-paper-field` moves onto `.app-layout` — the element App.vue owns and documents; `<body>` regains the right to carry §6.2's static boot-error region and a `<noscript>`; and main.ts becomes the single reader of the frozen `window.__VALUE_GROUND_BOOT__`, handing it to `createApp(App, { boot })` so App.vue CONSUMES the boot object as §6.2 requires and `resolveHydratedBootModel`'s duplicate precedence engine is deleted outright rather than kept in sync. ## ADDENDUM — App shell: the composition root, the one lattice, and the producer housing

**Normative.** The value.js demo has no composition root, and every structural defect in
`demo/color-picker/App.vue` is downstream of that fact or of one adjacent fact: the shell hand-rolls
a housing primitive glass-ui already ships.

1. **The entry is a module, not markup.** `demo/app/main.ts` is the sole composition root. It
   performs, in order: the one stylesheet import (`../styles/foundation.css`), `initGlobalDark()`,
   `createApp(App, { boot: window.__VALUE_GROUND_BOOT__ })`, `app.use(router)`,
   **`await router.isReady()`**, the app-level `provide`s (API client, always-on session ports),
   and `app.mount("#app")`. `demo/app/index.html` contains **zero inline executable script**: one
   external classic prepaint (`./prepaint.js`) and one external module (`./main.ts`). No component
   may perform app-level installs, import a stylesheet, or assume mount order. The `await
   router.isReady()` is normative, not stylistic: without it the first-rendered scene is not the
   final scene on 10 of 14 routes and the overture DAG stalls at B2 for the life of the session.

2. **The mount container is not the portal host.** `<body class="relative" data-paper-field>` keeps
   **both** attributes — they serve the body-portalled dialogs, which are the app root's siblings —
   and Vue receives its own `<div id="app">`. Exactly one attribute (`id`) moves. Proposals to
   delete `class="relative"` or relocate `data-paper-field` onto `.app-layout` are refused: one
   `position:absolute` direct child of `<body>` uses body as its containing block, and the field
   stamp must dominate four sibling portal hosts.

3. **`groundRecordInject`, `__GROUND_*__` and the TypeScript precedence engine die in one cut.**
   Per §6.2 the prepaint is an external classic script with no build-time token injection; the
   scheme defaults are canonical tokens in `--ground-seed-token-light` / `-dark`. `vite.config.ts`
   imports nothing under `demo/`. `boot/ground.ts` and `boot/hydrate.ts` are deleted; the app
   consumes the frozen boot object and never re-derives URL→storage→default. `useColorUrl` owns the
   live sync only.

4. **One route lattice.** `demo/shell/viewSchema.ts` is the single table. Routes derive from its
   keys; scene resolution is a `Record` over the closed union; dock metadata reads the same rows.
   `meta.admin` (five producers, zero consumers), the fourteen literal route rows, the
   `isViewId(name) ? name : "picker"` coercion and `componentFor`'s `return ColorPicker` catch-all
   are deleted. An unknown view is a navigation event, never a substituted render.

5. **Region composition is the producer's.** glass-ui 7.0.0 exports `InstrumentChassis` with
   `proportion: "golden" | "preview-dominant"`, `reserve`, a typed `boundaries` set, `#stage` /
   `#inspector` / `#action` slots, inspector-absent expansion, and a container-query collapse. Per
   `OPTICAL-BENCH-COMPOSITIONS.md` §5 seam 1, **value.js owns the route `<main>` and adds no grid
   CSS**. `.pane-container`, `.pane-container--dual`, `.pane-wrapper--left/--right/--ghost`, the
   `[data-layout]` display witnesses, the breakpoint `v-if` mount fork, `mobilePaneIndex`,
   `PaneSegmentedControl.vue` and `PaneSlot.vue` are deleted, not restyled. The shell's block axis
   becomes `min-height: 100dvh` with a sticky dock band; the document scrolls.

6. **The edge points down.** No shell module may name a leaf component's method. Workbenches publish
   their own action bar through `ACTION_BAR_KEY` (`demo/shell/actionBar.ts`); the shell injects.
   `usePaneRouter.ts` is deleted whole. `providePalettePorts` is split by lifetime — always-on ports
   at `main.ts`, browse ports at `BrowsePane.vue`, admin ports at `AdminPane.vue`. A provider whose
   scope exceeds its consumers' scope is a god module and is refused.

7. **The shell owns identity, not just landmarks.** One `<h1>` inside `<main>`, fed by the same

waveSpec.title: The shell tells the truth about what it mounted
waveSpec.scope:
demo/color-picker/ (entry, App.vue, composables/boot/*), demo/shell/ (PaneSlot.vue, useViewManager.ts, usePaneRouter.ts, viewSchema.ts, dock/), demo/styles/shell.css + the overture.css relocation, vite.config.ts (entry + ground seam), e2e/smoke/oracles/o4-order-invariance.spec.ts, docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/states.mjs. result.addendumClause: **V·§App-shell — route truth, slot truth, and shell identity.** The application entry is a module file. It installs the router, awaits `router.isReady()`, and only then mounts; no component may render a route-derived pane before the route is true, and no boot beat may be armed by a single DOM event without a state-checked floor. Pane-instance registration is reported by the slot that mounted the instance, never dispatched by a name a call site guesses; a slot that renders a pane registers it at every viewport, and a control the dock renders as named and enabled is live at every viewport or it is not rendered. The shell owns its route's sole `<main>`, exactly one `<h1>`, one bypass link as its first tabbable node, and one polite status region; it does not own a ratio, a stage/inspector split, a breakpoint mount fork, or any domain dialog. The document is the scroller. No masking fallback may stand between a lattice table and its consumer: unknown names are navigation events, not silent substitutions. Every one of these obligations is discharged by an executable gate that is RED against the tree it was written for; a gate with no input that reddens it is deleted, not weakened.
result.dissent:
AGAINST CHALLENGE-D, ON SEVERITY AND SCOPE. D-2 is upheld — the canon retires the two-pane workspace in five clauses and I read all five. But D-2's framing, that "every finding except D-5, D-6, D-9 and D-14 is a consequence of that one premise, which is why the cure is a transposition", does not survive the measurements. The two defects that actually break the product for a real user are NOT consequences of the two-pane premise. J-1 breaks on /#/gradient at any viewport, dual-pane or single, and would survive the single-scene transposition untouched because its cause is `router.isReady()` and an unfloored beat. J-2 would be MASKED by removing the breakpoint fork, not cured — the per-call-site `:on-mount` prop and the `any`-typed `currentConfig.left` dispatcher would still be there waiting for the next branch. Adjudicating this component as "the architecture is retired, therefore transpose" would ship a beautiful single-scene shell with a wedged boot DAG and a dead dock on mobile. Cut 1 and Cut 2 come first for that reason, and they are the two cuts that need no W18 ratification to land.

AGAINST CHALLENGE-D, ON EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE. Four of its sub-claims are refuted by bytes: D-15's "solid source-side fact" (foundation.css:678-695 contains .atmosphere-canvas at :683 and [data-glass-field-canvas] at :684, and my Chromium forced-colors run shows the shell chrome transforming correctly); D-13's verbatimModuleSyntax parenthetical (App.vue:164); D-12's API-violation charge (useViewManager.ts:59-70 — mobilePaneIndex is a writable computed, its setter IS the API); and D-9's URL-duplication arm (the prepaint script contains no URL read at all). Four refuted sub-claims in one report is the cost of arriving from a premise of guilt, and correcting it is what this seat exists for.

AGAINST CHALLENGE-C, ON C-7. The measurement is right and the mechanism is wrong. A cure written against the stated mechanism ("make the boot clamp a no-op write") would have landed, looked green on inspection, and left the address bar still rewriting — because useColorPipeline's clamp runs at App.vue:245, before useColorUrl's non-immediate watch is installed at App.vue:377. I have gated the observable instead and made "find the real writer" an explicit obligation of the wave.

AGAINST CHALLENGE-L, ON L-3'S CURE. Relocating `injectGroundTokens` to `plugins/vite-ground-tokens.ts` is the right shape of fix for the wrong tranche: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:172 retires `groundRecordInject` and `__GROUND_*__` BY NAME, in the same cut as the frozen boot object. Building the plugin would be building something the canon has already scheduled for demolition. The finding stands; the cure is retirement, folded into J-9.

WHERE I EXPECT THE OTHER JURORS TO DISAGREE WITH ME, AND MY POSITION. I graded J-5 (the retired architecture) BLOCKER but split its disposition BUILD + FOLD(W18), and I graded J-6 (50/50) MAJOR rather than BLOCKER. A design-axis juror will likely grade both BLOCKER and demand they land whole in this wave. I hold that VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:56 settles it against them: W18 must ratify one low-fidelity and one real-rendered composition PER MEMBER — "Picker cannot stand in for About" — before feature styling proceeds. This wave can honestly land the seam and exactly one ratified value (Picker's exact golden inspector 38.1966011%, :42) and no more. A wave that promised eleven compositions would be promising W18's work with W18's authority, and its gate would be unwritable — which is the same failure mode as a vacuous gate, arriving from the other direction.

TWO GATES I REFUSED TO WRITE, ON PURPOSE. A forced-colors gate would be GREEN at authorship (DIS-1) and is therefore vacuous. A blob-determinism gate would be flaky rather than sound, because I cannot name an input that reliably reddens it (HYP-2: both of my Chromium /#/ desktop runs produced the blob; the one tracked WebKit absence is a real context loss, not a demonstrated rate). Under born-RED law both must be deleted rather than weakened, and I deleted them. What survives from HYP-2 and IS gated is the byte-certain half: the blob has no context-loss contract anywhere in the tree, and B4 has only a success edge.

ONE UNSOUND GATE I FOUND IN MY OWN SUITE AND FIXED. G1b originally selected on `.picker-shell` — a token J-20 deletes. It would have gone RED after the wave because its own selector retired, not because the contract broke. Rewritten to assert "5 overture marks + ornament present" and re-verified RED.
